headline: Deep and metric learning models for microbial, phage-host and gut disease prediction
label: Machine Learning For Sequence Prediction
summary: Learned models are being evaluated on microbiome and phage-host data, where benchmark design and phylogenetic structure shape how reliable predictions are.
synthesis: The three items share a common thread of learned models applied to microbial and host-associated data, with evaluation design a recurring concern. A benchmark of network-analysis methods on GLV-simulated single-time-point microbial samples compares network-impact and individualized dissimilarity-overlap approaches against alpha- and beta-diversity measures and neural networks. A phylogeny-aware positive-unlabeled deep metric learning framework targets phage-host interaction identification, using host tree constraints to inform species-level prediction. AR-CDT Net applies a deep deformable convolutional network with CD-Tanh activation to gut microbiome-based disease classification across more than 8000 samples. The novelty lies in incorporating phylogenetic structure into the learning objective and in architectural modifications tailored to microbiome classification, rather than in generic model application alone.
